context.exploration_scope: First real-operational-mode Evolution run: Trigger checked first (E40 fixed baseline), Gate/Execution explicitly skipped (not merely empty) when untriggered; no new Evolution mechanism designed

problem: E44 closed Evolution's design/verification arc and declared the execution boundary ready for real operational use -- this had not yet actually been exercised as an operational (Trigger-first) run rather than a design/verification (always-run-everything) one.

decision.decision_summary: Trigger check (E40 baseline, E41..E44 logic reused verbatim): 0 real changes -- triggered=false. Gate and Execution explicitly SKIPPED (not run, not merely empty) -- no real change to react to. 0 code modifications.

action.action_summary: Fresh Trigger check against E40's fixed baseline; Gate/Execution conditionally skipped; Verification always run regardless of Trigger outcome; 0 new Evolution mechanism designed.

result.note: No real project change has occurred since E40 -- correctly skipped Gate/Execution rather than running them to find nothing, marking the real transition to Trigger-first operational mode.

cause.root_cause_summary: E44 closed the design/verification arc but every phase through E44 still ran the full pipeline regardless of whether a real change existed -- the actual Trigger-first operational discipline had not yet been exercised.

lesson: Operational mode is not just "the same checks, run again" -- it is structurally different: Gate and Execution are skipped, not exercised-and-found-empty, when there is no real Trigger. This is the real distinction between a design/verification phase and an operational one, and it is worth encoding explicitly rather than leaving implicit.
